The analysis concerns a rectangular beam cross-section of width b = 50 mm and height h = 120 mm.
The problem is modeled under small-deformation, linear-elastic Euler–Bernoulli beam theory, so plane sections remain plane and stresses vary linearly over the depth.
Units are N, mm, and MPa, so the bending moment M = 4,000,000 N·mm and dimensions are used directly.
The y-coordinate is measured from the neutral axis, which coincides with the centroidal horizontal axis, positive upward.
The applied moment M = +4,000,000 N·mm is sagging (positive) bending, producing compression at the top fiber and tension at the bottom fiber.
The centroid lies at mid-height, so the extreme fibers are at y = +60 mm (top) and y = −60 mm (bottom).
The area moment of inertia about the neutral axis is I = b·h³/12 = 50 × 120³ / 12 = 7,200,000 mm⁴.
The governing relation is the elastic flexure formula σ(y) = M·y / I, valid for 0 ≤ |y| ≤ 60 mm.
The maximum bending stress magnitude is σ_max = M·(h/2)/I = 6·M/(b·h²) = 33.33 MPa.
The bending stress at the top fiber (y = +60 mm) is σ = −33.33 MPa (compressive).
The bending stress at the bottom fiber (y = −60 mm) is σ = +33.33 MPa (tensile).
The bending stress at the neutral axis (y = 0 mm) is σ = 0 MPa.
The stress distribution is linear in y, varying from −33.33 MPa at the top to +33.33 MPa at the bottom, passing through zero at the neutral axis.
Material elastic constants (E, ν) are not required for the stress calculation because flexural stress in the linear-elastic range is independent of E; if deflections were later requested, an E value would be needed.
Report the stress values σ(y) at y = 0, +60, and −60 mm, along with the governing relation σ(y) = M·y/I and the linear stress profile.
